fields.meta_title: Personal Landing Page Builder From a Prompt | Emergent
fields.meta_description: A personal landing page gives visitors one person and one next step. See how a speaker, a founder, a professor, and a coach each built theirs.
fields.h1: Build a Personal Landing Page With One Clear Next Step
fields.hero_description: Build a personal landing page with your story and one request form, and keep every reply in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Behind Your Name
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the page a visitor reads about you, plus the form and the emails that handle what they send.
fields.feature_1:
A page written from one description

Describe who you are, who should find you, and what they should do next. Emergent builds the page and its request form, then changes either one when you send another prompt.
fields.feature_2:
Every request saved as a row

Each request lands as a row in a database you own, with every answer in its own column and the time it arrived. Sort the table by any answer, or search it for one name.
fields.feature_3:
Rules that pick who reads it

Write a rule in plain words, such as investor notes go to my cofounder. The app emails each matching request to the person you named and keeps everything else in your own list.
fields.feature_4:
Connected to the tools you use

Connect the page to any tool with an API, such as HubSpot or Slack. A new request can become a contact in your CRM or a post in a Slack channel, without copying it by hand.
fields.feature_5:
Your name as the web address

Publish the page on a domain you own, such as your full name. The link on a slide or a business card then reads cleanly. Custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits.
fields.feature_6:
The code is yours to take

Export the page and its code to your GitHub repository on paid plans, then keep building it in your own tools. Building and publishing are both covered on the free tier.

fields.usecase_heading: Personal Landing Page Examples by Role
fields.tab_content_1:
A 650-person kickoff goes straight to her agent

Event planners who find Halima Rennick give her page three answers: the event date, the city, and the audience size. Any event of 300 or more people is emailed to her agent, Oren Tasker. A 650-person sales kickoff in Denver reached him the morning it came in. Smaller events wait in Halima's own list.
fields.tab_content_2:
Dmitri sees any press deadline under 48 hours

Reporters reach Brightkiln founder Jules Pemberly through a press page with her bio beside her headshots. The form asks for the outlet, the request type, and the deadline. A press request due in under 48 hours is emailed to her chief of staff, Dmitri Kilbride. Podcast invitations and later deadlines wait in his Monday list.
fields.tab_content_3:
Two Thursday slots are still open by Tuesday

Students book Selin Vaughan from the page that lists her papers on coastal wetlands. She offers eight 15-minute office hours slots each Thursday, and the page drops a slot once a student books it. By Tuesday this week, six were taken. The two still open were 2:30 and 2:45 PM.
fields.tab_content_4:
29 people asked for help with a career change

Every intro call request on Camille Desrosiers's page starts with one question: what do you want next? The app saves each answer with the request. Of September's 54 requests, 29 named a career change and 16 a promotion. The other 9 came from people planning a return to work.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Personal Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to a personal landing page that asks for one kind of request and routes each one to whoever should answer it.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Decide what one visitor should do
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Add proof a visitor can check
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Ask only what you act on
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pick the one request the page exists for, such as a speaking inquiry or an office hours booking. A page with a single action is easier to scan and easier to measure. Move every other link to the footer or to a separate page.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Say who you help and how, in words a stranger understands: "I give keynotes on hiring to sales leaders." Put that line under your name at the top. Leave the full career history for a profile or a resume, and link to it once.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Show evidence that fits the request. A speaker lists talk titles with past events, a researcher lists papers, and a coach quotes clients in their own words. Name real events and dates, because two specific items say more than a wall of logos.
fields.howto_step_4_des: List the answers you need before you can reply to a request, such as the date and the city for an event. Each question should change what you do next. Cut any field you would read and then ignore, and keep the form short enough to finish on a phone.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Write a rule for each kind of request before you build. Some go to an agent or an assistant by email, some wait in a weekly list, and the rest come to you. Name the person and the condition, such as anything due within a day.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Describe the page in one prompt
fields.howto_step_6_des: Tell Emergent who the page is for, then add the form questions and the rules from step 5. The first build includes the page and a table that stores each request. Read that version closely, then change a line or a field with another prompt.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Send one test request for each rule and confirm it lands where the rule says. Then publish the page on your own domain (built into Emergent, uses credits) and put the link where people already look for you: your email signature, your slides, your profiles.

faq_plan.q: What is a personal landing page?
faq_plan.a: A personal landing page is a single web page about one person that asks visitors to take one action, such as sending a speaking request or booking office hours. It sits between a full website and a social profile: short enough to read in a minute, with a form that turns interest into a request.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a personal landing page?
faq_plan.a: Decide the one request you want, then write two lines about who you help. Add proof, and keep the form to the questions you act on. With Emergent's AI landing page builder, you describe all of that in one prompt, and Emergent builds the page with a table that keeps every request.

faq_plan.q: What sections should I borrow from personal landing page examples?
faq_plan.a: Borrow four: your name with a two-line introduction, a recent photo, proof that fits the visitor, and one form. Each of the four examples on this page is built around a single form, such as a speaking request or an office hours booking, and leaves everything else off the page.

faq_plan.q: How is a personal brand landing page different from a personal website?
faq_plan.a: A personal brand landing page has one goal, while a personal website holds your writing and your history across several pages. Start with the landing page when you want a specific request, and hold it to the same standard as any high converting landing page: one headline, one action. Add the website later if your writing needs room.

faq_plan.q: How do I write the introduction for an about me landing page?
faq_plan.a: Write who you help, what you do for them, and one proof point, in that order and in under 100 words. Use first person and plain verbs: "I coach engineers moving into management." An about me landing page should end with the one action you want, such as an intro call form.

faq_plan.q: How long should a personal landing page be?
faq_plan.a: Keep it to what a visitor can read in about a minute: an introduction, two or three proof points, and the form. Each extra section should help the visitor decide to send a request. If you have more to say, link once to a profile or a resume instead of adding sections.

faq_plan.q: Where does a video introduction go on a personal landing page?
faq_plan.a: Put it next to the form, below your two-line introduction. A visitor then hears you right before they decide to send a request. A 60-second clip suits spoken work, such as talks or coaching. If the video is the main event, build a video landing page around it instead.

faq_plan.q: How do I keep my personal landing page up to date?
faq_plan.a: Update it whenever your offer changes, such as a new talk or a full calendar. In Emergent, you send a prompt like "add my October keynote to the talks list," and Emergent changes the page. Requests saved before the change stay in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: What should the button on my personal landing page say?
faq_plan.a: Name the request in the visitor's words: "Request a talk" or "Book office hours." Use one button label across the page, and point every button at the same form. On a page Emergent builds, every submission lands in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: How do I make my personal landing page work well on a phone?
faq_plan.a: Test it on a phone before you share the link. Keep the form to a few fields that fit on one screen, make the button wide enough to tap with a thumb, and put your name and introduction at the top. The same checks apply to any mobile landing page.

plan.angle: Searchers want personal landing page examples and a way to make one about themselves. The pages that rank show galleries of templates; none shows what happens after a visitor acts. This page shows four people whose single page does one job each (a speaker taking event requests, a founder fielding press, a professor running office hours, a career coach sorting intro calls) and follows every request to the person or list it reaches. It stays off the sibling ground: no work galleries (portfolio), no music (artist), no job applications (resume), no client service menus (freelancer), no link menus (link in bio). The FAQ covers the definition, building one, what good examples share, a personal brand page versus a full site, what an about me page says, length, video, keeping it current, the call to action and phones.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build a Personal Landing Page With One Clear Next Step'; hero 'Build a personal landing page with your story and one request form, and keep every reply in a database you own.' covers the whole job, under 130 chars.

intent.evidence: Four role examples (speaker, founder, professor, coach) under 'Personal Landing Page Examples by Role', a 7-step how-to, and a comparison table match the examples/how-to intent of the primary and 'personal landing page examples'.

specificity.evidence: 'Any event of 300 or more people is emailed to her agent, Oren Tasker'; 'Of September's 54 requests, 29 named a career change and 16 a promotion.'

openers.evidence: Every paragraph opens on a full sentence: 'Event planners who find Halima Rennick give her page three answers', 'Describe who you are, who should find you, and what they should do next.'

craft.evidence: Varied sentence lengths, no tacked-on endings; QC Q5/Q7 clean. 'request' repeated 22 times noted.

voice.evidence: 'Name the request in the visitor's words: "Request a talk" or "Book office hours."' reads operator-written; no AI tells.

truth.evidence: Emergent claims map to claims_used (free-start: 'Building and publishing are both covered on the free tier'; custom-domain: 'Custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits'); table generated from library; tab numbers agree (29+16+9=54; 8 slots, 6 booked, 2 open).

distinct.evidence: Request-routing angle per role stays off portfolio (galleries), artist, resume, freelancer and link-in-bio ground; the career-coach tab is intro-call sorting, unlike the coaching page's executive/team/group/sales tabs.

faq.evidence: 10 on-topic questions, answer-first, secondaries 'personal landing page examples', 'personal brand landing page', 'about me landing page' each worked in once; hub link in item 2; links to high-converting, video and mobile landing page pages.
